summary: Blue sky with numerous fair-weather cumulus clouds; scattered puffy white clouds, horizon and ground visible, no precipitation.
caption:
caption: This high-resolution image captures a section of the troposphere featuring various cumulus clouds set against a vivid blue sky. The clouds exhibit characteristic low-altitude, puffy structures with distinct, rounded tops and relatively flat bases, indicating the condensation level where rising parcels of moist air have reached their dew point. The brilliant white color of the clouds is a result of Mie scattering, where larger water droplets scatter all wavelengths of visible light equally. In contrast, the intense blue of the surrounding sky is caused by Rayleigh scattering, the process by which shorter wavelengths of sunlight are scattered by the small molecules of the atmosphere. The varying luminosity and shading within the clouds highlight the three-dimensional volume and the interaction between incoming solar radiation and the clouds' optical thickness.
